questions.explain: Natural rubber from Hevea latex is cis-1,4-polyisoprene; the cis double bonds kink the chains and make it elastic. The trans polymer is gutta-percha, which is hard and non-elastic.
Bu = butadiene, Na = sodium (the original catalyst), N = nitrile from acrylonitrile. Butadiene + styrene gives Buna-S.

questions.q: Which of the following rubbers is a condensation polymer?
questions.explain: Thiokol forms from 1,2-dichloroethane and sodium polysulphide with elimination of NaCl. The diene rubbers are addition polymers.

questions.q: During vulcanisation of natural rubber, the sulphur cross-links form mainly at
options: The allylic C–H positions next to each C=C
The C=C carbons, by adding across every double bond
Aromatic rings in the polymer chain
questions.explain: Heating with sulphur at about 373–415 K builds –S–S– bridges at the reactive allylic sites, so chains can no longer slide past one another and the rubber becomes stronger and less sticky.
